transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-01-26
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Maya Ortiz, Samir Patel, Hannah Li (Redwood); Priya Shah, Liam Carter, Angela Ruiz, Jordan Kim, Ben Torres (NexaHealth)

Summary: quick weekly sync to check onboarding progress and confirm env readiness for perf bench.

[00:00] Maya Ortiz: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i think we can get started - we've got about 45 minutes. maya from redwood here, samir is on the line for the infra bits.
[00:08] Priya Shah: hey maya, thanks. quick heads up - we got some people dialed in from security and devops to knock out the network items.
[00:15] Samir Patel: awesome. quick agenda - onboarding checklist, service account/iam, vpc peering, dataset access and then next steps for the perf benchmark. sound good?
[00:23] Liam Carter: yep sounds good. last week i started the service account but ran into a permissions question, so want to align on minimal perms.
[00:30] Maya Ortiz: perfect, liam. we documented minimal IAM in the checklist - it's basically storage read for the dataset, secretsmanager get for tokens if you use secrets, and compute/network for the peering test. i'll resend the exact policy.
[00:42] Jordan Kim: uh, real quick - the sample dataset we're going to use, is that de-identified? we need to ensure PHI is not present.
[00:50] Hannah Li: yes that's important - the sample we provide is synthetic and scrubbed, it's the same set we used in the last benchmark. we'll attach the dataset link in the follow-up.
[01:05] Angela Ruiz: on the security side, i looked at the SOC2 summary you sent but have follow-ups: how does key management work, do you allow customer-managed KMS, and what audit logs are available?
[01:18] Maya Ortiz: good Q. we support customer-managed KMS for private deployments and dedicated - we can enable CMEK. hosted has KMS integration but the key management model depends on the plan; i'll get the security doc that spells it out. audit logs are available at the route/token level in the console, and you can forward them to your SIEM via syslog or S3 export.
[01:36] Angela Ruiz: ok please share the doc. also need to know retention windows and whether logs show token-level input - we need to evaluate data exposure.
[01:45] Samir Patel: one note on logs - we can mask or redact inputs at ingest if you prefer, or set up a forwarder that only ships metadata. i'll include that in the security follow-up.
[01:58] Priya Shah: thanks. liam - what's the current state of VPC peering?
[02:03] Liam Carter: i've opened the ticket with infra, i have the CIDR ranges ready but i need the firewall ports. which ports do we need open for the peering?
[02:12] Samir Patel: for the initial connectivity test we need TCP 443 outbound from your peered subnet to our service endpoints, and we recommend allowing the ephemeral port range 1024-65535 for the flow. i'll paste the exact list in the checklist.
[02:27] Ben Torres: is there egress required from our side to s3 or something for the sample dataset?
[02:31] Maya Ortiz: yes if you host the sample on your s3 we will request an IAM role or presigned url. alternatively we can host the sample on a secure redwood bucket and grant read-only access, whichever you prefer.
[02:45] Jordan Kim: for perf, what's the expected qps and concurrency we should plan for?
[02:50] Samir Patel: we normally parameterize the perf run. from the POC intake you indicated target 200 qps at p95 latency <= 300ms for short prompts. can you confirm?
[02:58] Priya Shah: that's the ballpark. for a start, 100-200 qps is fine. we care more about p95 than p99.
[03:06] Maya Ortiz: ok we'll aim for 100-200 qps; samir will publish the pre-benchmark checklist and baseline infra requirements.
[03:12] Hannah Li: timeline note - we suggested running the 2-hour perf window week of Feb 8 to give time for network + keys. does that still work?
[03:19] Liam Carter: yes that gives us a week to provision. i'll try to have peering and service account done by Jan 29.
[03:26] Angela Ruiz: regarding KMS, are you able to support a customer HSM? our compliance team might ask about that.
[03:33] Maya Ortiz: for private deployments yes, we have HSM/KMS integrations; for dedicated we offer CMEK with cloud KMS, and on prem we can support HSM integrations. i'll loop in our security engineering doc and a contact for deeper KMS conversations.
[03:46] Priya Shah: great. another item - we saw a mention of quantization in the docs. will that affect model outputs for our clinical NER workload?
[03:54] Samir Patel: good question - quantization can change some tokenization edge behaviors. for high accuracy use-cases like NER, we typically recommend testing both fp16 and int8 quantized variants in the benchmark; we'll include quality regression checks against your eval set.
[04:12] Jordan Kim: perfect, we'll prepare an eval set of about 500 examples with expected labels.
[04:18] Maya Ortiz: awesome. i'll include an eval harness template in the repo.
[04:25] Ben Torres: any blockers on our side besides service account and peering?
[04:30] Liam Carter: maybe firewall and also we need to coordinate a time for the benchmark during low traffic window.
[04:35] Maya Ortiz: understood. for timing samir will propose 2-3 slots during the week of Feb 8.
[04:40] Hannah Li: quick question on billing/quotas - how do we handle token usage during a POC?
[04:44] Maya Ortiz: for POC we provide a capped trial usage tied to the deal id. if you need more tokens for bench we can temporarily bump it; we'll send a simple PO if needed.
[04:52] Angela Ruiz: and retention - where does data persist and for how long?
[04:56] Maya Ortiz: for hosted inference logs are retained 30 days by default; for dedicated/private we can configure retention per contract. again we'll include that in the security packet.
[05:05] Priya Shah: ok that's helpful. one more item: can we get a short architecture diagram showing traffic flow for hosted vs dedicated vs private?
[05:12] Samir Patel: yes we have diagrams - i'll attach the dedicated vs hosted vs private flow graphic in the follow-up.
[05:18] Priya Shah: great, thanks.
[05:22] Maya Ortiz: recap of open items: maya to send checklist + security docs; samir to send firewall/ports + perf checklist; liam to provision service account and peering; angela to compile security questions. we will tentatively target perf week of Feb 8. any objections?
[05:36] Liam Carter: no objections.
[05:38] Angela Ruiz: none from security.
[05:40] Jordan Kim: all good.
[05:43] Maya Ortiz: cool. we'll follow up with a short email and Jira-style action items. thanks everyone.
[05:49] Priya Shah: thanks all.

References shared during call:
- Onboarding checklist (link): https://redwood.example.com/onboarding/checklist (shared in chat)
- SOC2 summary & KMS doc: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2-kms.pdf
- Perf harness repo (template): https://git.re/bench/harness (note: placeholder)

End of transcript.
